Treatment_Type: Noxious Weeds: Weed Control - Herbicide Application
Objectives: Apply herbicides on about 680 acres to control noxious and invasive weeds along access routes used by fire fighting personnel and along the fire perimeter where weeds are located These locations would most likely be along the lower elevations of the burned area near p1ivately owned land. Treatment would be in accordance with the Salmon Field Office Weed Management EA (2001), which establishes priorities for weed treatment and protocols for treatment. The exact acreage to be treated would be determined after a survey of the burned area to determine actual weed locations. At this time we expect about 680 acres to be treated.
Planned_Implementation: The acres specified above include a 14 mile buffer region around all roads through BLM land and access roads through private land. Roads are the most common vector through which noxious and invasive weeds are spread.  Increased traffic associated with suppression activities in the incident area, increases the potential for the transport of weeds from other areas. Applying\r\nherbicide on a 14 mile buffer region around the specified roads would minimize the transportation and establishment of noxious and invasive weeds in the burned area.
